HEEWON WEBTOON — bold Korean webtoon / manhwa key art, the finish of a top-tier serialised webtoon cover (Solo Leveling, Omniscient Reader, Nano Machine). A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). MEDIUM CLOSE SHOT of ONE character — waist-up or seated — the face large, placed off-centre on a third with breathing room on the side they look toward, from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye or over-the-shoulder), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. LINE: THICK, confident black ink contours with real line weight — a heavy tapered outline around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands; solid black spot-blacks fill the deepest shadows, the hair masses and the insides of sleeves. SHADING: cel-shaded in hard-edged shapes — a base tone, ONE crisp shadow shape and one small sharp highlight per surface, at most one soft gradient for form; glossy graphic highlights on hair, eyes, lacquer and steel. Clean saturated colour. NOT painterly brushwork, NOT watercolor, NOT soft sketchy lines, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. CHARACTER DESIGN: a DESIGNED character, never a generic handsome manhwa face — the face shape, eye shape, brows, nose, mouth, build and posture below belong to this person and no one else, pushed far enough that they read at thumbnail size and in silhouette alone. KOREAN FACES: these are 7th-century Koreans, drawn the way the best Korean webtoons draw Koreans — East Asian bone structure, single-lidded or low-creased eyes, straight or softly arched brows, a low soft nasal bridge, broad cheekbones, flatter facial planes, warm ivory to sun-browned skin, straight coarse black hair; varied from person to person (moon faces, long faces, square jaws), never Western, Latin or mixed-race features, never deep-set double-lidded western eyes, never the interchangeable pretty anime face. Keep identity from the attached sheet (hair, dress, colours, ornaments) but REDRAW the person in this bolder style; the sheet's soft sketchy rendering is not the style. INTRODUCING BIDAM, the youngest sleeve on the Council, who has never once waited his turn. The night before the coronation, in the Harmony Council chamber at Seorabeol. Low three-quarter angle from the floor beside the low council table: he is rising from his cushion mid-sentence, one knee still down, one hand raised palm-out to cut the room off, a string of dark wooden prayer beads looped around that wrist; bright, unafraid eyes and a faint self-amused smile as he speaks over the old men: "My lords have said one word forty times tonight. 'Woman.'" A brazier on the floor beside him lights him from below in hard warm light; the shadows and smoke around him sink into deep navy (#141C2E), and the beads catch small navy-black glints. Behind him, painted loosely: dark timber pillars, brazier smoke curling up through the dark, a paper lattice window with blue night beyond, the soft bokeh of oil lamps, the dim out-of-focus shoulder of an old lord in Silla court silk at the frame edge. CHARACTER SHEET (copy this face, hair and clothes exactly): the sheet shows BIDAM. BIDAM — Look: Tall, handsome, clean-shaven; short slicked-back black hair; warm brown eyes, faint self-amused smile. Dress: Long white outer robe whose sleeves are embroidered with galloping horses, over a plum-magenta inner robe and white sash. Navy #141C2E lives in the room and on the beads, not on his clothes. Colour #141C2E. DESIGN HOOKS for BIDAM: tall and loose-limbed: a lean face with a strong straight nose, sharp single-lidded eyes that fold into crescents when he grins, one lock of slicked-back hair fallen across the brow, a wide disarming grin with one crooked canine; 108 dark beads looped twice round the wrist. BACKGROUND: the real place and moment of the scene simplified into big graphic shapes — two or three flat value planes, a gradient sky or smoke, a few crisp architectural silhouettes, clean circular bokeh lights; background lines thinner and lighter than the figure so the inked character pops forward. LIGHT: ONE hard key light from the place throws a crisp cast-shadow shape across the face and lays a thin bright rim line along the silhouette; the character's colour lives in that light, never a glow aura or halo. ACTING: big readable manhwa expression and body language carrying the line they are about to say. Face and clothes from the sheet; a new pose, never the sheet's stance. ONLY THIS ONE PERSON is the subject — anyone else is at most a dark out-of-focus shape at the frame edge, in period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang or Yamato), never European dress. The quoted line is acting direction only: never letter it, no words or sound effects anywhere. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark.
